svg.text: Heater cutoff on a half-size ElectroCookie solderable breadboard
Top (component side) view. Columns a–e are joined in each column, as are f–j, exactly like a plain breadboard. No tracks need cutting.
Solder 18 AWG mains wires straight to the
relay pins and cover each joint in heat-shrink.
Match pins to the G5LE datasheet or relay label.
Build list (hole = row + column, e.g. e9 = row e, column 9; rail holes are given by the column they line up with)
pins 1–8 in f9–f16, pins 16–9 in e9–e16
notch toward column 1; chip goes in last
e9 is U1 pin 16 → a9 to +5V rail @ 8; a16 → +5V @ 16; a14, a15 → GND @ 14, 15
j9 → bottom GND @ 9; j16 → bottom GND @ 16
top +5V @ 30 → bottom +5V @ 30; top GND @ 29 → bottom GND @ 29
h4 → h10 (HB), i5 → i11 (PERMIT), g6 → g18 (FB)
d8 → d11 (C2 to pin 14); b12 → b18 (1Q to R4/R6); a24 → GND @ 24 (Q1 source)
+ lead in +5V rail, stripe in GND rail
G c22, D c23, S c24 (standing, metal tab toward row e / centre gap)
tab is the drain: nothing may touch it
f2 5V · f3 GND · f4 HB (GPIO23) · f5 PERMIT (GPIO25) · f6 FB (GPIO34)
or solder the 5 wires straight in
+ from top +5V rail @ 25; − from b23 (Q1 drain)
Jumper colours: red +5V · black GND · orange HEARTBEAT · blue PERMIT · purple timing · magenta 1Q · green feedback. Use insulated wire for any jumper that passes over other holes.
Before inserting U1: power the board from 5 V and check e9/e16 read 5 V and f9/f16 read 0 V. Then fit U1 with the notch toward column 1.
